claims.text: Instrumented nanoindentation mapping of FeNiCrMn will reveal significant local heterogeneity in hardness and elastic modulus.
The local mechanical-property heterogeneity is masked by conventional bulk tests.
FeNiCrMn has a standard, cost-effective formulation.
FeNiCrMn can be fabricated by powder metallurgy or additive manufacturing in the proposed initial state.
The fabricated FeNiCrMn alloy is predominantly a single-phase solid solution.
The fabricated FeNiCrMn alloy contains inherent microstructural variations.
Nanoindentation mapping will be performed across the sample surface at room temperature under quasi-static loading on a predefined indentation grid.
Local grain-boundary differences, nanoscale precipitates, or segregation mediate local mechanical-property variations in FeNiCrMn.
The spatial resolution of nanoindentation captures localized mechanical responses.
Grain boundaries or secondary-phase regions respond differently during nanoindentation and produce a distribution of hardness and modulus values.
Conventional bulk tensile, compressive, or microhardness tests average out local mechanical-property variations.
Nanoindentation mapping will show statistically significant spatial variations in FeNiCrMn hardness and elastic modulus.
Some mapped regions will have hardness approximately 10–20% above or below the mean bulk value.
An unusually homogeneous microstructure could make local property differences too small to detect.
Insufficient spatial resolution could prevent reliable detection of local property differences.
The magnitude of local property variations depends on processing route and sample preparation.
A standard deviation of less than 5% relative to bulk-test values would falsify the proposed significant microscale heterogeneity.
